A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Ada-KV work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results and proofs.

before.justification: v4 reports original Ruler and LongBench evaluations, attention-output loss measurements, and memory and decoding-latency results.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds relative-budget evaluations, larger-model results, newer-method comparisons, and parameter-sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain global attention-weight selection, adaptive head budgets, safeguard mixing, and Top-k eviction. GQA handling and cache implementation remain unchanged. The additional integrations do not document a revised allocation procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same 13 Ruler tasks and 16 LongBench datasets under question-aware and question-agnostic compression. The added models, budgets, and comparisons use retained task coverage.

E2.justification: v5 Table 3 substantially extends comparisons to DuoAttention, HeadKV, and CriticalKV and DefensiveKV with and without Ada-KV. SnapKV, Pyramid, StreamingLLM, and full-cache comparisons remain in the original experiments.

E3.justification: Alongside the retained evaluation settings, v5 introduces relative LongBench budgets of 10%, 20%, and 40%, Llama-3.1-70B evaluations at 20% and 40%, and newer-method comparisons at those latter budgets. Appendix A.3 also introduces an alpha sweep; these are additional protocols, not established reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 and Table 4 test safeguard sensitivity using alpha values 0, 0.2, and 0.5 on Mistral-7B across four LongBench budgets. Earlier loss measurements, subtask analyses, and head-concentration visualizations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The added sensitivity table reports scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v5 Tables 1–4 add substantial results under new settings. At 20% budget, SnapKV/Ada-SnapKV averages are 41.29/42.87 for 8B and 44.95/46.08 for 70B. Newer-method and alpha-sensitivity scores are also added. The original detailed LongBench values remain unchanged in v4 Tables 2–5 versus v5 Tables 5–8.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, eviction-loss bound, and Theorems 3.1–3.3 remain unchanged. Their proofs match between v4 Appendices A.6–A.8 and v5 A.8–A.10; equations are combined and renumbered.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: head-wise adaptive allocation, its loss-bound foundation, plug-and-play integration, and benefits under both compression scenarios. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v5 adds a rationale about fixed-budget bias across unequal sequence lengths, recommends greater emphasis on question-agnostic evaluation, and explicitly identifies the within-layer allocation limitation. Appendix A.3 adds an alpha tradeoff interpretation, although its statement that smaller alpha permits more aggressive allocation conflicts with unchanged Algorithm 2.

D1.justification: v5 omits v4's explicit StreamingLLM settings of four sink tokens and recent-window retention. Its efficiency caption newly specifies that all methods use FlashAttention-2. The main code link, default parameters, CUDA/cache-layout details, and GQA implementation remain.

R1.justification: Section 5 substantially expands positioning relative to follow-up adopters and training-based head allocation, including DuoAttention and HeadKV. Section 2.2 relocates and expands v4's appendix discussion of sparse attention. New quantization and speculative-decoding references are added, while Quest is removed.

P1.justification: Most core prose remains close to v4. v5 rewrites the LongBench discussion, subdivides related work, introduces Section 5, and moves references before the appendix. Author and citation formatting also change, and unresolved reference placeholders appear.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single-column layout. v4 Figures 1–2 are redrawn and combined into v5 Figure 1; other plots are resized or rearranged. New tables are added, and retained detailed result tables are compressed to two per page. The removed main-text result table remains represented in the appendix.

improvement.justification: The added relative-budget, 70B, and newer-method evaluations strengthen evidence for scalability and broader compatibility beyond v4, while the explicit limitation clarifies scope. These gains are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: the alpha interpretation conflicts with Algorithm 2, and Section 5 overstates superiority to DuoAttention—Table 3 gives CriticalKV with Ada-KV 48.00 versus DuoAttention 48.17 at 40% budget. The net improvement is therefore limited.
